newsitem.title: USA: SF Fed Parry says higher dlr no fix for inflation.
newsitem.headline: SF Fed Parry says higher dlr no fix for inflation.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Robert Parry said on Tuesday the stronger dollar cannot be a permanent fix against U.S. inflationary pressures.
"Inflation seemingly is in abeyance," Parry told the Salt Lake City Rotary Club in a speech made available in New York.
Parry noted the good inflation news coincided with strong growth in output and the lowest unemployment rate in decades.
The San Francisco Fed president attributed the good inflation performance to several factors, such as U.S. companies' cost-cutting efforts and the dollar's rise.
Parry said the stronger dollar has been "helping to hold down the price of many imports."
"But, again, this isn't a 'permanent fix' against inflationary pressures," Parry said. "After all, we can't expect the dollar to keep appreciating forever."
Parry warned that transitory factors, such as the dollar's rise, and fundamental improvements alike, "don't add up to a claim that inflation is dead and we need not be watchful about it anymore."
